I still remember the day I optimized a slow-performing ETL pipeline by 40% just by replacing self-joins with window functions - it was a game-changer. 
Here are a few window function tips that I wish I knew earlier: 
Use RANK() to assign a unique rank to each row within a result set, partitioned by a specific column.
Leverage LAG() to access data from a previous row, which is super useful for calculating differences or percentages.
Utilize LEAD() to peek into the next row, handy for forecasting or identifying trends.
Mastering these window functions can take your SQL skills to the next level, especially when working with large datasets in tools like dbt or Apache Spark.
